Not move, because the surface tensions are equal
Flow from the smaller alveolus into the larger one
Flow out of both alveoli equally

H⁺ ions formed in brain ECF from CO₂ that crosses the blood–brain barrier

Deoxygenated blood can carry more CO₂ than oxygenated blood
Bicarbonate leaves red cells in exchange for chloride
CO binds haemoglobin with 240 times the affinity of O₂

stem: As the force of a voluntary contraction is gradually increased, motor units are recruited
options: From the smallest (slow, fatigue-resistant) to the largest (fast, fatigable)
From the largest to the smallest
All at once, with force graded only by firing rate
explanation: This is Henneman's size principle: small motor neurons have high input resistance and reach threshold first. Force is graded by both recruitment and rate coding. For the first few seconds of intense effort, ATP is regenerated from phosphocreatine.
